facts.text: Signal Hill earned its name from the massive white fieldstones arranged as the numerals 113, 51, 151, and 137, erected in 1915‑16 to honor World War I battalions.
The stone numerals rise up to 36.5 meters tall and 3.7 meters wide, making them the largest rock‑art military commemorations in Canada.
Signal Hill was once called Cairn Hill before the 1982 renaming, a nod to the stone cairns that marked the site.
The Visitor Centre, opened in 1991, now hosts interactive exhibits that bring the hill’s communications and military history to life.
During the First World War, Sarcee Camp on Signal Hill trained more than 45,000 Canadian Expeditionary Force soldiers, the largest training centre in Alberta.
Signal Hill’s battalion numbers were created by soldiers as a spirited competition, each unit carving its regimental badge into the hillside as a conditioning exercise.
